title: Early Digital Shield and Parental Mental Health
summary: In the first two years of life, a child's brain grows at the fastest pace of their whole life, through real human interaction and sensory play. WHO’s 2019 guidelines recommend no sedentary screen time for infants or one-year-olds. The updated AAP policy, published in January 2026, focuses on content quality, family needs, prioritising sleep, play, physical activity and reading, and shared media engagement. It states that infants do not learn from digital media and that occasional brief, high-quality videos are not detrimental; this does not recommend routine infant viewing. These guidelines do not promise to prevent speech delay or diagnose a child’s condition. At the same time, the mother's mental health needs care: telling the passing 'baby blues' apart from postpartum depression, and the spouses sharing the load to prevent burnout and chronic exhaustion.
try_this: This week: agree as a couple to make the baby's room completely free of screens and digital distractions. Set a flexible schedule for sharing night-time care so the mother gets at least 4 hours of unbroken sleep to restore her mental and physical energy.
reflection_prompts: What natural alternatives (talking, singing, sensory toys) will you offer your child instead of playing videos?
How can we notice and deal with postnatal exhaustion together, as one team?
